reading.body:
CyrusOne's Sterling campus publishes 116 MW of IT capacity across three facilities, placing it second among Virginia data centers with disclosed specs and representing 7.2% of the state's declared IT load.

The campus spans 1.18 million square feet of technical space, which at 116 MW implies approximately 98 watts per square foot. This power density is consistent with mixed workloads rather than optimized AI training deployments. The operator has published no certifications or specializations for this campus. At typical mixed-workload density of 400 kW per rack, the facility could accommodate roughly 290 racks, which at 8 GPU accelerators per rack would equal approximately 2,320 accelerators if fully deployed for AI. That is a theoretical maximum not necessarily reflected in actual operation.

Virginia's 330 mapped data center facilities include only 25 with published capacity figures. This opacity matters for grid planning because the state's total AI-capable compute footprint remains unknown. Sterling's contribution to Virginia's aggregate 1,603 MW of declared capacity is measurable, but whether this campus constrains or supports AI scaling depends on grid availability and actual workload composition, neither of which are published.
